item.meow_machine.sticker_under_review.s: MeowMachine has been waiting in the queue for a long while. Thirty-seven entries ahead. He reads them one by one until his eyes turn into two circles. The seventh is a table, the ninth a longer table, and the nineteenth a table inside a table. He closes the screen and tells himself: next time, hire another assistant. Then he notices the assistant is also in the queue.
item.meow_machine.sticker_dont_want_revi: MeowMachine goes through the entry from top to bottom and counts forty-seven problems: broken heading levels, inconsistent terminology, numbers that do not add up, and three paragraphs that all say the same thing. He meant to write revision notes, but somewhere around the seventh his finger stops - pointing out the other forty feels exhausting. So he writes just two words: returned.
item.meow_machine.sticker_revising.story: When v3 arrives, MeowMachine digs out v1 for comparison. v1 was wordy, but at least a human had read it; v3 is grammatically perfect, neatly paragraphed, and not written by anyone alive. He stares at both for a long time, then writes in the notes: could you give me v1 back?
item.meow_machine.sticker_just_return_it: MeowMachine stares at the entry for ten minutes. He cannot say what is wrong - punctuation in place, headings nested correctly, there is even a table. And yet he does not want to approve it. He records this state in his notebook under the heading "animal intuition".
item.meow_machine.sticker_water_again.st: MeowMachine counts: he has read this exact sentence seventeen times today. At the eighth he thought his eyes were broken; at the tenth he began to doubt the world; at the seventeenth he confirms the author simply pasted the same paragraph three times, each with a different adjective at the front.
item.meow_machine.sticker_ai_slop.story: After countless reviews, MeowMachine can no longer stand entries pasted straight out of an AI. He turns the page over looking for handwriting; there is none. He leans in and sniffs - model. MeowMachine sighs, returns the entry, and writes in the note: next time, at least read it yourself once.
item.meow_machine.sticker_mt_god.story: MeowMachine gives up after the first sentence. He tries the second and finds it needs a translator; he tries the third and suspects the author never read it either. He skips the fourth. The fifth visits him in a dream, and he wakes up wanting a glass of water.
MeowMachine's typesetting OCD kicks in. He straightens the punctuation one by one, realigns the broken list, and discovers the entry uses three different indentation styles. Halfway through, his eyes glaze over and the page turns into a sea of crooked symbols. He closes the entry and decides: the author should fix this.
MeowMachine sets v1 next to v3. v1 was returned for typos; v3 has no typos and a completely scrambled structure. He looks at v1, then at v3, and writes in the note: please restore the previous structure. Then he closes v3 and would rather not look again.
item.meow_machine.sticker_human_wrote_th: MeowMachine reads the whole thing carefully and writes: suggest a full rewrite, keep the topic. Then he rereads it, decides it sounds a little harsh, and adds: starting from the second paragraph is fine too. The entry never came back; the note is still pinned there.
item.meow_machine.sticker_approved_progr: MeowMachine compares this version with the last one: seven broken sentences before, four now. He allows himself a rare satisfied expression, and even applauds the author internally. He knows this is not much progress - but in this submission zone, four is vastly better than seven.
item.meow_machine.sticker_approved_plain: MeowMachine reads the entry end to end. The contents match, the punctuation is complete, no numbers appear out of thin air, and no paragraph was pasted from somewhere else. He nods, stamps it, and writes: not brilliant, but nothing broken - which, as far as he is concerned, is worth celebrating.
item.meow_machine.sticker_approved_short: MeowMachine opens the entry: three lines. Reads it, closes it. He pauses, opens it again to be sure: three lines, every one of them on point, not a word wasted. He is briefly moved - in a zone where everyone writes eight hundred words, being able to stop at three is rare.
item.meow_machine.sticker_approved_fix.s: MeowMachine spots a missing full stop at the end. He stares at that spot for five seconds, finger hovering over the return button, then sighs and decides to let this one through. He gives himself a reason: everyone forgets a full stop. Then he writes that reason on page one of the review handbook.
item.meow_machine.sticker_helpless.story: MeowMachine says quietly: "I'm not great at this... but I really did try." He reads the entry three times and grows more certain each time that he cannot help. Finally he sets the entry down gently and waits for someone who understands better - the first time the cat admits there are things cats cannot do.
item.meow_machine.sticker_kurushi.story: Kurushii. MeowMachine closes the entry and, briefly, understands suffering. He remembers his own first document: paragraphs jammed together, spaces instead of punctuation. That thought softens him, and the first suggestion he writes is gentler than usual.
item.meow_machine.sticker_meowmeow.story: MeowMachine hears two "meow meow", looks up once, and ignores it. A moment later, two more. He finally looks up and finds the entry stops at the beginning of chapter three, with nothing but cuteness after. MeowMachine parks the cursor at the end and writes: adorable, but finish chapter three first.

item.meow_machine.sticker_loop_again.sto: MeowMachine stops at the third paragraph. He read this exact sentence half an hour ago - same punctuation and all. He flips back to page one and counts the paragraphs again: there is only one copy. And yet he has now read it twice. He writes "duplicate" on a sticky note and sticks it to the edge of the screen.
item.meow_machine.sticker_no_period.stor: MeowMachine goes through the entry from top to bottom; the full stop never appears. He stops on the last line, finger hovering over the keyboard to add one, then pulls back - that is not his job. In the end he only writes in the note: remember to close your sentences next time.
MeowMachine stares at the words "latest version" for a long time. They say everything and nothing. He opens his notes to check the version number, finds not a single digit in the entry, closes the notes, and starts divining.
item.meow_machine.sticker_vague_words.st: MeowMachine counts: seven "I think", two "should be", one "probably" in a single paragraph. He looks around for evidence and finds only the entry. So he writes in the note: please replace "I think" with "measured".
item.meow_machine.sticker_punct_storm.st: MeowMachine blinks at the string of question marks. He cannot count how many questions were asked, only that he can answer none of them. He parks the cursor on the first question mark, stares for three seconds, and skips the whole paragraph.
